body: Friday, August 21 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed held rates steady this week, but FOMC minutes revealed officials saw a need for a rate hike if inflation doesn't cool — a distinctly hawkish hold. Fiscal stress is the dominant macro variable: the 30Y yield topped 5.31% (highest in 19 years) earlier this week, forcing Treasury Secretary Bessent to intervene with buyback operations. The 10Y sits at 4.73% and is edging higher (+5 bps vs 4W). The 2Y at 4.19% (prior close) is falling (−18 bps vs 4W), producing a +50 bps 2s10s curve — positively sloped but still flat by historical standards, a configuration where the long end holds up on fiscal/term premium risk while the front end prices Fed patience. VIX at 15.33 is down 17.5% vs 4W, indicating complacency despite bond turmoil.

New / Most Important: This week's defining event was the Treasury buyback announcement, which the market treated as a circuit-breaker for long-end yields. Bond yields gave back "almost all gains" from the intervention by Friday, per Yahoo Finance — the buyback relief was fleeting. The Iran conflict escalation pushed oil prices and yields higher mid-week, with Trump threatening "Economic D-Day" sanctions. FOMC minutes explicitly flagged hike risk, shifting the modal path from "higher for longer" to "possibly higher still." Bitcoin surged 23.7% over 4 weeks, rallying past $77,000 specifically on the Treasury buyback announcement — the market is treating crypto as a fiscal-debasement hedge. Gold at $4,686 is up 15.2% vs 4W, confirming the same debasement/fear trade. China's record July loan contraction and a 12.4% plunge in US housing starts underscore that this is not a growth-led rally but a capital-flight-from-sovereigns story.

Playbook ✓: Equity resilience despite bond stress follows the playbook of liquidity-driven rallies where Treasury operations inject fungible reserves — S&P at 7,683 (+3.7% vs 4W) and Nasdaq 100 at 29,337 (+4.3%) confirm mega-cap tech absorbing flows as a duration proxy. Russell/Nasdaq ratio declining 1.4% confirms narrow leadership.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The structural break here is that Treasury buybacks are now being used as a de facto monetary policy tool, independent of the Fed, to manage term premium — and the market is front-running their insufficiency. This is a new regime: the fiscal authority is conducting quasi-QE (buying back off-the-run Treasuries to improve liquidity) while the monetary authority is threatening to hike. The two arms of policy are pulling in opposite directions, which is why gold and bitcoin are simultaneously surging — they are pricing the logical impossibility of fiscal dominance coexisting with hawkish monetary policy. The fact that the buyback relief in yields lasted less than 48 hours tells you the market needs a far larger intervention. If the Treasury is forced to shift issuance dramatically toward the front end (bills) to avoid term premium blowouts, it will effectively re-run the 2023 Yellen playbook, injecting liquidity into risk assets while long-end yields remain structurally elevated. This is the most important macro dynamic globally right now: the US is losing control of its own yield curve through fiscal channels.

Macro Stance: The ECB is on hold with a hawkish tilt. Kazāks stated the ECB is "well placed to act if needed" to reach 2% inflation, while the euro gained on hawkish ECB outlook. European borrowing costs hit record highs on Iran war inflation fears.

New / Most Important: Goldman Sachs highlighted European stocks defying global shocks with strong earnings growth — a relative value story that matters. European sovereign yields are elevated alongside US yields, but the euro is strengthening, suggesting relative confidence in ECB credibility vs. the Fed/Treasury confusion.

Playbook ✓: European equities outperforming on valuation catch-up and earnings delivery is consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The euro strengthening despite firm US dollar recovery is notable — it suggests FX markets are pricing ECB hawkishness as more credible than Fed hawkishness, possibly because the ECB doesn't face the same fiscal dominance problem. If US Treasury buybacks are read as proto-debasement, capital rotation toward European fixed income and equities could accelerate.

Macro Stance: Monetary policy has handed the baton to the budget. China kept loan prime rates steady for a 15th month (Reuters, [Aug 19]), the 1-year at 3.0% and the 5-year at 3.5% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 19]), and liquidity runs through the overnight window, with 7-day reverse repos at zero for seven straight sessions (BigGo Finance, [Aug 19]). The yuan is the pressure point. It surged to 6.72 per dollar, a 42-month high (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]), while the PBOC fixed the reference rate at 6.7808, weaker than the previous fix (CryptoRank, [Aug 20]) and well above the 6.7262 Reuters estimate (investingLive, [Aug 20]): a deliberate brake that follows its move to slow yuan gains (Bloomberg, [Aug 19]). Prices leave room to ease: July CPI rose 0.5% and PPI growth slowed to 3.5%, both missing expectations (BigGo Finance, [Aug 8]).

PMIs & Activity: July's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2 and non-manufacturing to 49.0 (FXStreet, [Jul 31]); the private factory gauge eased to 50.9 (Fibre2Fashion, [Aug 3]), a four-month low (Reuters, [Aug 2]), and private services growth was the slowest since September 2024 (Reuters, [Aug 4]). The hard data confirmed the slide: industrial output grew 4.5% y/y and retail sales just 0.6% (Reuters, [Aug 17]), output, retail sales and investment all missed forecasts (The Business Times, [Aug 17]), and fixed-asset investment fell 6.7% in the first seven months (Xinhua, [Aug 17]). Exports remain the engine, up 23.9% on high-tech shipments (The Asian Banker, [Aug 14]). The regional August flash readings split: Japan's manufacturing PMI jumped to 55.1 on chip and AI orders (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]) while Australia's composite slipped from a six-month high (TradingView, [Aug 20]), a pattern that rewards China's tech supply chain, not its domestic demand.

Credit Impulse: July new bank loans posted a record contraction as credit demand faltered (Reuters, [Aug 14]), only the second contraction this year (The Standard (HK), [Aug 14]), yet Bloomberg reports credit growth exceeded forecasts despite the rare loan slump ([Aug 14]). Reconciled: headline financing, which includes bond issuance, beat; bank lending to households and firms shrank, leaving cumulative yuan loans up 10.38 trillion yuan in January–July (Xinhua, [Aug 14]). The new interest subsidies target exactly that gap by cutting the effective cost of SME and consumer borrowing without touching the LPR. The bond market reads the impulse as weak: Chinese bonds bucked the global selloff (CNBC TV18, [Aug 19]) with the 10-year near a one-year low (TradingView, [Aug 19]).

Property: July new home prices were stagnant as demand stayed weak (Reuters, [Aug 17]) and first-tier prices were flat, ending a four-month rebound (South China Morning Post, [Aug 17]). Bloomberg says prices fell at a faster pace ([Aug 17]), while the 70-city index fell 3.2% y/y, the smallest drop in five months (BigGo Finance, [Aug 17]): the annual comparison eased as the monthly decline deepened. Property investment slumped nearly 20% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 17]) and land sale revenue posted its biggest drop in a decade (finance.biggo.com, [Aug 18]). The response is city by city: Shanghai is lowering second-home down payments (South China Morning Post, [Aug 20]). Evergrande's founder was jailed for life and the firm fined $2.4 billion (Asia Financial, [Aug 20]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: China pledged timely fiscal support to bolster growth (Reuters, [Aug 20]), the vice finance minister promising more policy support in a timely way (TradingView, [Aug 20]), and widened fiscal interest subsidies, raising the SME loan cap to 75 million yuan and covering credit-card instalments for the first time (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]). Trade is fragmenting along bilateral lines: China urged the US to immediately withdraw its drone tariffs (Reuters, [Aug 20]), agreed a deal with Switzerland scrapping most levies (Bloomberg, [Aug 20]), and wields new legal powers against the EU as talks near (Bloomberg, [Aug 20]), while rare-earth exports critical to US aerospace rose (Reuters, [Aug 20]).

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng climbed 0.80% to 25,698 (BBN Times, [Aug 20]) but A-shares fell across the board with the Shanghai Composite down 0.32% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]) after ChiNext tumbled 6.26% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 19]), leaving stocks headed for weekly losses (TradingView, [Aug 20]). Mainland capital pulled a net HK$10.4 billion from Hong Kong stocks (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]), and materials names are emerging as new market leaders (Bloomberg, [Aug 20]). Beijing debuted offshore government bond futures to promote yuan use (Nikkei Asia, [Aug 20]) as China cut US Treasury holdings to an 18-year low (Benzinga, [Aug 18]).

New / Most Important: The fiscal pledge is the answer the LPR did not give. By subsidising SME and consumer interest through the budget, Beijing lowers the cost of credit where demand is weakest while sparing bank margins and avoiding a rate cut that would fight its own brake on a yuan at a 42-month high. It is targeted support, not a package, and July's loan contraction says demand rather than price is the binding constraint.

Playbook ✓: Rates on hold, fiscal subsidies, city-level property easing and a managed yuan are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Markets expected July's miss to force rate cuts; Beijing answered with subsidies and a firmer yuan, so China exports strength and imports weakness. Iron ore rose only as China demand concerns met stimulus hopes (TradingView, [Aug 18]) and Fortescue still hopes for a swift return to normal China trade conditions (Reuters, [Aug 19]); the Australian dollar weakened as PMIs failed to impress (Mitrade, [Aug 20]). Europe is turning confrontational, with Germany's finance minister saying China is "not playing by the rules" (Bloomberg, [Aug 20]), as European exporters face a buyer that takes less and sells more. Oil at $86.91, down 2.7% in four weeks, is a smaller import tax but no demand signal.

Macro Stance: Japan's inflation picked up this week, backing the BOJ's case for a rate hike. Multiple sources — Bloomberg, FT, BeInCrypto — now characterize a September BOJ hike as increasingly unavoidable. Mizuho's markets head expects the BOJ to raise rates "soon and more often." The yen is in a self-reinforcing cycle where weakness drives inflation which drives hike expectations which strengthens the yen.

New / Most Important: Friday's CPI print confirmed accelerating inflation, making a September hike the base case. The structural overhang of Takaichi's BOJ appointments in 2027 looms — signaling potential political interference with tightening pace. Japanese corporate bond issuers face a new hurdle from rate hikes, per Global Finance Magazine.

Playbook ✓: BOJ normalization continuing as inflation becomes self-sustaining is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: This is the single most dangerous cross-border flow mechanic in global markets right now. BOJ rate hikes unwind the yen carry trade — the largest funding trade in the world. Every basis point of BOJ tightening pulls capital back to Japan from US Treasuries, Australian RMBS, EM local debt, and European credit. The fact that this is happening simultaneously with US fiscal stress and Treasury buyback interventions creates a toxic feedback loop: Japanese institutions repatriate capital → US long-end yields rise further → Treasury forced into more buybacks → more debasement signal → more gold/BTC bid. Takaichi's 2027 BOJ appointment timeline means the market has roughly 12-18 months of genuine BOJ hawkishness before a potential political pivot. The "self-fulfilling cycle" language used by CryptoRank is apt — yen strength begets more yen strength, and the unwind has barely begun.

Macro Stance: The RBA held rates at its recent meeting but the hawkish rhetoric intensified significantly. Deputy Governor Hauser explicitly warned the RBA "will have to raise rates again if inflation doesn't come down." Bendigo Bank is tipping a November rate hike.

New / Most Important: The RBA flagged AI mania as an inflation driver that could push up interest rates — a novel and structurally interesting framing where asset price inflation from tech speculation feeds into demand-side overheating. Softer jobs data provided some offset but hasn't changed the hawkish tilt.

Playbook ✓: AUD holding near highs on tightening bets is consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The RBA calling out AI-driven inflation is genuinely novel among G10 central banks. If AI capex spending creates wage pressure in tech-adjacent sectors and wealth effects drive consumption, the transmission mechanism from Silicon Valley to Australian monetary policy is real — Australia's superannuation system means equity gains feed consumer spending more directly than in most economies.

Macro Stance: Inflation has reaccelerated and the RPP is holding, with Commerzbank warning that the slow hawkish shift weighs on the zloty. The data flow of the last two days hardened that stance: GUS reported enterprise wages up 6.8% y/y in July with employment down 0.8% (Do Rzeczy, [Aug 20]), and industrial output up 5.1% y/y (PAP Biznes, [Aug 20]) with construction lagging (xyz.pl, [Aug 21]). Parkiet called the wage beat a cold shower for the RPP [Aug 20], although PKO BP's economists argue labour data will not drive the council's decisions (wnp.pl, [Aug 20]). The price side offers no relief: core inflation is at a ten-month high (Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 14]), German producer prices point to higher inflation ahead (Parkiet, [Aug 21]) and Strefa Biznesu notes both the ECB and the RPP hold with further moves tied to price pressure [Aug 19]. ING flagged today's August PMI and expected Fitch to leave the rating unchanged [Aug 21].

Markets: The week closed with a relief rally built on results. Dino was the star of the session (Parkiet, [Aug 21]), up 5.5% with the WIG20 gaining 1% (Bankier.pl, [Aug 21]), breaking out of its downtrend (Comparic.pl, [Aug 21]); Tauron was weakest (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 21]), and Orlen rose with oil after Trump's threats as PZU moved on results (FXMAG, [Aug 21]). Thursday had been the mirror image, with KGHM leading the declines (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 20]). The card, struck before today's bounce, shows the reset: EPOL 44.17 (+0.5% 1W, +8.3% 4W); banks lead, PKO 113.7 (+3.9% 1W, +6.0% 4W) and Pekao 259.6 (+1.8% 1W, +11.5% 4W), Orlen 156.0 (+3.3% 1W) recovered, while the energy-CIT losers sit at the bottom, PGE 10.2 (-6.8% 1W, -3.8% 4W) and KGHM 332.45 (-6.6% 1W, +10.1% 4W), with LPP 20,700 (-4.3% 1W), Allegro 44.62 (-3.9% 1W) and Dino 32.29 (-1.3% 1W) before today's jump. The zloty is the strong leg for external reasons: the dollar is the cheapest in months after Washington's move (Bankier.pl, [Aug 21]) and USD/PLN is testing 3.69 with the euro below 4.32 (Comparic.pl, [Aug 21]); the card has USD/PLN 3.6918 (-1.2% 1W, -3.0% 4W) and EUR/PLN 4.3146 (+0.1% 1W, -0.4% 4W). On POLGBs, Hungarian bonds now yield less than Polish ones (Subiektywnie o finansach, [Aug 20]) and Business Insider Polska argues AI firms competing for capital are lifting Poland's debt-service cost [Aug 20].

Fiscal & Politics: Two external verdicts arrived on the day the tax bill was published. Fitch affirmed Poland's rating (Gov.pl, Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 21]) and S&P Dow Jones Indices upgraded Poland to developed-market status (Reuters, [Aug 21]), which Domański welcomed (Business Insider Polska, [Aug 21]); Rzeczpospolita adds that S&P's reaction to the PIT and CIT changes lets the government breathe [Aug 21]. The draft itself is bigger than the headline PIT relief: Portal Samorządowy counts over 50 billion zł for public finances [Aug 21], Gazeta Prawna reports a rate rising from 19 to 22% among further changes from 2027 [Aug 21], the ministry confirmed a new tax to raise 4.8 billion zł (Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 21]) that mirrors the 4.8 billion zł of power-price relief for energy-intensive industry (Gov.pl, [Aug 21]), and Rzeczpospolita estimates Orlen, PGE, Enea and Tauron will add close to 7 billion zł to the budget [Aug 21]; ING Think calls the package fiscally neutral [Aug 20]. Tusk called an extra cabinet sitting on taxes (Polskie Radio 24, [Aug 21]) after the budget meeting (PAP, [Aug 21]) and Gazeta Prawna still sees a possible Nawrocki veto [Aug 21]. The deficit exceeded 141 billion zł after seven months (Bankier.pl, [Aug 17]) and defence spending is to reach 5% of GDP by 2027 (TodayPress.tv, [Aug 21]).

Corporate & Sectors: Dino's Q2 brought 400 million zł of net profit and 3176 stores (StockWatch.pl, [Aug 21]), revenue of 18 billion zł with 148 openings and capex near 1 billion zł (Omnichannel News, [Aug 21]) and guidance for a gradual LFL recovery in the second half (Bankier.pl, [Aug 21]); pb.pl's verdict is that the absence of disappointment sufficed [Aug 21]. KGHM's half-year EBITDA rose 89% y/y (Strefa Inwestorów, [Aug 21]) on 5579 million zł of net profit (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 20]); the CEO set out expansion into the US and Africa with a possible listing (wnp.pl, [Aug 21]) and it is borrowing 1 billion zł for Sierra Gorda (Polski Przemysł, [Aug 21]). The 30% energy CIT is now a dividend question for Orlen and Unimot (StockWatch.pl, [Aug 21]) and Parkiet sees pressure on utility results [Aug 21]; PGE and Ørsted finished all 111 Baltica 2 monopiles on schedule (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 21]). PKO BP won KNF approval for portfolio management and set a new target (Bankier.pl, [Aug 21]) while Franknews.pl warns of over 68 thousand repaid CHF contracts open to challenge [Aug 21]. CD Projekt rose ahead of its Gamescom showcase (INNPoland.pl, [Aug 21]); XTB won Indonesian CFD approval (TradingView, [Aug 21]).

Geopolitics & Security: Tarcza Wschód has reached initial operational readiness in many places after two years (Strefa Obrony, [Aug 21]) and the MON says the border can be mined within 48 hours (Interia Wydarzenia, [Aug 21]). Thursday's mass strike on Ukraine saw Polish jets scrambled and RCB alerts in two voivodeships (Radio ESKA, [Aug 20]); Romania says Russia's strikes increasingly spill into NATO (ABC News, [Aug 21]) and the US deployed a surveillance aircraft to Poland (Firstpost, [Aug 21]).

New / Most Important: Reclassification to developed-market status and a Fitch affirmation on the same day the government publishes a 50 billion zł tax package is the best possible sequencing for the sovereign and the worst for the utilities. The agencies have judged the package neutral, which anchors POLGBs and the zloty, but the money is raised from the sectors the WIG20 leans on, so the index is being re-weighted from Orlen, PGE and KGHM toward banks and domestic retail. Inflation reaccelerating removes any near-term easing optionality, and 6.8% wages confirm it.  |  Playbook ✓: Sticky CEE inflation is consensus; stay long banks and Dino, underweight the energy-CIT payers, keep duration short and treat the zloty bid as a dollar story.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Developed-market status arrives with a president threatening to veto the budget's funding mechanism: the index providers are upgrading the market while the politics that fund it are unresolved.

Macro Stance: EM currencies hit a record high as traders dialed back Fed hike expectations. India featured prominently with Yahoo Finance highlighting "investment opportunities in India" and the rupee active around 95.70. Argentina's Vaca Muerta shale attracted US billionaire capital, per Yahoo Finance.

New / Most Important: US Treasury buybacks may redirect capital toward Asia (Nation Thailand), creating a structural flow tailwind for EM Asia. The DXY recovery above 99.50 from a two-month low provides a partial offset.  |  Playbook ✓: EM FX strength on Fed pause is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Argentina receiving billionaire direct investment flows into shale is a structural shift — Vaca Muerta becoming a capital magnet represents a real-asset alternative to US shale at a time when Iran tensions make non-Middle-Eastern hydrocarbon sources strategically valuable.

Narrative: Mega-cap tech keeps absorbing global flows as the safe-haven equity trade, with the Nasdaq 100 up 4.3% vs 4W; the AI capex cycle remains the driver and Nvidia's earnings next week headline the calendar.

Reported: Keysight beat by $0.59 with revenue above estimates (Investing.com, [Aug 18]), and analysts boosted forecasts after the upbeat Q3 (Benzinga, [Aug 19]). Fabrinet beat on strong data-centre growth (Zacks Investment Research, [Aug 18]) but tumbled despite an upbeat Q1 outlook (Seeking Alpha, [Aug 18]). Xiaomi's profit fell after the memory crunch hit smartphone demand (Bloomberg.com, [Aug 18]).

EPS Upside Watch: CrowdStrike — Benchmark says it could beat Q2 expectations across the board (Stocktwits, [Aug 18]); the stock then sank 7% despite a Truist target raise (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 19]), resetting the bar. Snowflake — RBC sees software earnings beats with Snowflake leading the pack (Finimize, [Aug 14]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: A $4.68B fund dumped Nvidia and bought Warner Bros., a sign some institutional money sees the AI hardware trade as fully priced and is rotating into content and IP — a view that gains weight if Nvidia's guidance shows margin pressure from competition.
Narrative: Communications rides the mega-cap bid and AI-adjacent positioning; Stripe's OpenRouter deal signals a new race to control AI economics, with implications for platform monetization.

Reported: China's platforms disappointed. Baidu's revenue miss sank its shares as its CEO vowed to return Ernie to the AI frontier (Reuters, [Aug 18]); Kuaishou's earnings dropped by a third, hit by AI and creator costs (Bloomberg.com, [Aug 19]); NetEase fell as a Q2 earnings miss overshadowed stronger revenue (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 20]).

EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet — Google Cloud's backlog hit $514 billion in the same quarter capex guidance was raised to $205 billion (The Motley Fool, [Aug 16]): booked demand that converts into cloud revenue. AT&T — gaining as Verizon loses a customer battle, a share shift the market has not fully priced.

⚡ Breaking Convention: AI is a cost line before it is a revenue line: Baidu and Kuaishou show that platforms without compute to sell pay for AI out of margins, so the AI-adjacent bid should favour sellers of cloud capacity over pure ad and content platforms.

Narrative: A positively sloped but still flat curve (+50 bps 2s10s) is only modestly positive for bank NIMs, while surging long-end yields create unrealized losses on bond portfolios — the SVB dynamic.

Reported: Klarna dropped 19% after cutting its full-year guidance (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 18]) as German retail weakened (Reuters, [Aug 18]). Nubank's quarterly income hit $1 billion for the first time (American Banker, [Aug 14]). National Australia Bank's fiscal Q3 cash earnings rose, but its shares fell 4% (MarketScreener, [Aug 16]).

EPS Upside Watch: HSBC — RBC raised its price target as earnings forecasts climb (Proactive financial news, [Aug 17]). Canada's big banks — set to report strong results again, though valuation is the open question (Yahoo! Finance Canada, [Aug 20]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The curve is steepening for the wrong reasons — the front end pricing cuts, not growth — so banks gain little on NIM while carrying duration risk in held-to-maturity books. P&L and balance sheet tell opposite stories: shorter-duration money-centre banks win, regionals with underwater long bonds lose.
Narrative: Iran tensions drive the sector: Trump's "Economic D-Day" threat lifted oil mid-week, yet WTI at $86.91 is down 2.7% vs 4W as the US rig count reaches its highest since March 2025.

Reported: Santos beat first-half profit estimates and sees second-half output rising (Reuters, [Aug 18]). Ithaca Energy raised its 2026 dividend guidance after record North Sea production (Yahoo Finance UK, [Aug 19]). Energy Transfer raised its 2026 guidance (The Motley Fool, [Aug 16]).

EPS Upside Watch: Refiners — posting record profits (Investor's Business Daily, [Aug 14]). ExxonMobil and Chevron — oil profits have more than doubled, and an escalating Iran war is the swing factor for both (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 17]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Oil down 2.7% over four weeks despite a war threat says the market doubts a sustained Iran disruption, with soft demand as China's July industrial output slowed to 4.5%. Energy equities outperforming the commodity show investors prefer the cash-flow story — oil majors reaped a $93 billion windfall from the Iran war (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 16]).

Narrative: Reshoring capex supports the sector — Hyundai is considering expanding its Georgia Metaplant to 800,000 units — while American Airlines slid as rising oil prices added pressure (Quiver Quantitative, [Aug 20]).

Reported: Deere soared after its construction unit drove an earnings beat (Investopedia, [Aug 20]). Maersk raised its 2026 guidance as Q2 earnings surged (Ships & Ports, [Aug 14]). Curtiss-Wright raised guidance again (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 15]).

EPS Upside Watch: Quanta Services — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 14]) for the grid and data-centre contractor. Expeditors — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 18]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: AI is lifting industrial valuations toward tech's (Barron's, [Aug 20]): power and automation names now trade as growth stocks, so they would take tech-style losses if AI capex wobbles, while airlines still trade on oil — the sector is two trades, not one.

Narrative: Rising yields and elevated oil prices pressure the consumer, while wealth effects from surging equities and crypto cushion upper-income cohorts; retail earnings split winners from losers on execution.

Reported: Home Depot beat and reaffirmed guidance despite "frozen housing market conditions" (CNBC, [Aug 18]), and the stock rose (Barron's, [Aug 18]). Ross Stores raised its annual profit forecast again on discounted apparel demand (Reuters, [Aug 20]). Advance Auto Parts plunged 21% as a revenue miss overshadowed its earnings beat (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 20]).

EPS Upside Watch: H&M — analysts raised their forecasts ahead of the results (Il Sole 24 ORE, [Aug 18]). Amazon — Morgan Stanley raised its target to $500, seeing AWS revenue reaching $1 trillion in the AI era (Moomoo, [Aug 18]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Off-price split on execution, not demand: Ross jumped (Investor's Business Daily, [Aug 20]) while a "self-inflicted" slowdown clouded TJX's beat (Reuters, [Aug 19]). The weak consumer shows up first in footwear — JD Sports cut its profit outlook as US sales dropped (Reuters, [Aug 20]).
Narrative: Defensive staples underperform in a risk-on tape, and food-supply policy — the PRIME Act and USDA trending on X — could become a consumer-price story.

Reported: Walmart tumbled 9% after its outlook disappointed (CNBC, [Aug 20]) on its weakest sales growth in over six years (WSJ, [Aug 20]). Estée Lauder jumped 11.8% on a sales beat (StockStory, [Aug 19]). Coty fell as it warned of a "transition" year ahead (Bloomberg, [Aug 19]).

EPS Upside Watch: Target — analysts boosted forecasts after an upbeat Q2 (Benzinga, [Aug 20]), and it received almost $1 billion in tariff refunds that it plans to use to lower prices (Modern Retail, [Aug 19]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Tariff refunds are flattering the quarter: Walmart is using $2.9 billion of them to lower prices (CBS News, [Aug 20]), yet its shares still sank. One-off cash reinvested in price buys share, not margin, so staples beats this season need a refund-adjusted read.
Narrative: Defensive growth with rate sensitivity; Aveanna Healthcare ending a four-year rate fight is a positive template for reimbursement disputes across home health.

Reported: CSL rallied 18% on its earnings beat (Livewire Markets, [Aug 17]) as cost cuts beat target and FY27 guidance cleared the bar (Kalkine, [Aug 20]). Basilea raised its 2026 earnings guidance (MarketScreener, [Aug 18]). Hengrui saw profit growth squeezed by China's bulk-buying programs (Reuters, [Aug 19]).
EPS Upside Watch: Merck — upgraded at Morgan Stanley even as RBC downgraded (Seeking Alpha, [Aug 20]). GeneDx — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 19]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Price pressure at home is pushing Chinese drugmakers up the value chain: innovative drugs topped 60% of Hengrui's H1 revenue (BigGo Finance, [Aug 19]) even as bulk buying squeezed profit growth — more competition for global pharma pipelines, not just for generics.

Narrative: Copper at $6.59, up 4.2% vs 4W, is bid as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal, gold miners are shining with gold at $4,686, and materials remain the consensus beneficiary of the debasement plus AI-capex trade.

Reported: BHP's profit topped estimates as copper powered growth, with its highest dividend in 4 years (Reuters, [Aug 17]), copper now its growth "engine" amid the data centre boom (This is Money, [Aug 18]). SQM rose after an earnings beat and a higher lithium outlook (Reuters, [Aug 19]). Lundin Mining cut its copper outlook as Chile storms struck again (Mining.com, [Aug 19]), tightening supply for grid and data-centre demand.

EPS Upside Watch: Kaiser Aluminum — its H2 2026 update justifies a price target raise (Seeking Alpha, [Aug 20]). Gold miners — poised to outshine gold (ETF Database, [Aug 18]), with margins levered to gold at $4,686.
